# Explore mathematics. Learn through code.

Bringing programming and computational thinking
into university mathematics education.

CTM brings together European universities to
explore how computation can support mathematical
understanding, teaching, and learning.

::::: {.ctm-section}

## What is CTM?

**Computational Thinking makes sense of Mathematics
(CTM)** is a European collaborative project focused
on integrating programming and computational
thinking into university mathematics education.

The project aims to identify teaching needs,
develop practical educational resources, and
support students and educators across Europe.

:::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .ctm-card}

### 01. Understand

Identify challenges, needs, and effective
approaches to teaching mathematics with programming.

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .ctm-card}

### 02. Develop

Create tutorials, exercises, and mathematical
projects that support computational thinking.

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .ctm-card}

### 03. Share

Make educational materials accessible and
support their use across European universities.

:::

::::

:::::

## Mathematics Education in the Age of AI

Generative AI is changing how students
learn programming and approach mathematical
problems.

As teaching practices evolve, computational
thinking remains important for understanding,
evaluating, and applying computational methods.

[Explore AI & Education](ai.qmd)

:::

::::: {.ctm-section .ctm-section-light}

## From Ambition to Impact

CTM was designed to make programming and
computational thinking more accessible in
university mathematics education.

Its work was organized around several
connected areas, from identifying teaching
needs to developing educational materials
and exploring assessment strategies.

The sections below describe the project's
planned areas of work. Verified results
and materials will be added as they
are reviewed.

:::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}

::: {.ctm-card}

### 01. Understanding the Needs

Investigating student and educator
experiences, existing practices,
and obstacles to introducing
programming into mathematics teaching.

:::

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}

::: {.ctm-card}

### 02. Developing Tutorials

Planning accessible programming
tutorials and mathematical learning
activities that support
computational thinking.

:::

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}

::: {.ctm-card}

### 03. Creating Mathematical Projects

Developing approaches to computational
exercises and projects that connect
mathematical theory with applications.

:::

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}

::: {.ctm-card}

### 04. Exploring Assessment

Investigating ways to evaluate
students' computational work
and support meaningful learning
through programming activities.

:::

:::

::::

:::::

::: {.ctm-section}

## Looking Ahead: Mathematics Education and AI

Generative AI is changing how students
interact with programming and mathematics.

This development creates opportunities
and challenges for teaching computational
thinking, assessing student understanding,
and developing new educational practices.

[Explore AI & Education](ai.qmd){.ctm-button-outline}

:::

::: {.ctm-section .ctm-partners}

## A European Collaboration

CTM brings together five university partners:

- Lund University, Sweden
- Aalborg University, Denmark
- Technical University of Denmark
- University of Oslo, Norway
- Ruhr University Bochum, Germany

:::
